samasa.sense: when offerings (food, and in Purāṇic worship also animal victims) are presented to the deity

samasa.literal: in the work of the fire
samasa.sense: at a homa or fire ritual
at a great feast of the Goddess; महत् becomes महा in a karmadhāraya

morph.note: उद् + √चर्, causative उच्चारय- ‘to make go up, to utter’; with ण्यत् (-य) and loss of the causative suffix: उच्चार्य ‘to be uttered aloud’. The d of उद् is assimilated to c (उच्चर्).
From the causative श्रावय- of √श्रु: ‘to be caused to be heard’, i.e. to be recited for others to hear. The pair उच्चार्यं श्राव्यं covers reciting oneself and having it heard.

mantras.anvaya: बलिप्रदाने पूजायाम् अग्निकार्ये महोत्सवे (च) मम एतत् सर्वं चरितम् उच्चार्यं श्राव्यं च एव।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four locatives of occasion, then a subject (चरितम्) with two gerundives as predicate.
mantras.lit: At the presenting of offerings, at worship, at the fire rite, at a great festival — this entire story of my deeds is to be recited aloud and indeed to be made heard.
mantras.tr: At every offering, at worship, at the fire rite and at great festivals, this whole story of my deeds should be recited and heard.
mantras.tr_note: श्राव्यम् strictly means ‘to be made heard’ (recited for others); ‘heard’ keeps the line simple.

comm.t: The Devī names the occasions at which her whole story (सर्वं चरितम्) should be recited: the giving of bali, worship, the fire rite and great festivals. The emphasis on सर्वम् asks for the complete text, not excerpts.
The tradition reads the verse as the basis for reciting the Saptaśatī within every major Śākta rite, and for the homa in which its mantras are offered into the fire (the caṇḍī-homa).

Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra; so also वह्निहोमं तथा.

samasa.sense: worship in which bali is offered
samasa.alt: Some take it as a dvandva, ‘offering and worship’; but an itaretara dvandva would be dual and a samāhāra dvandva neuter, while बलिपूजाम् with कृताम् is feminine singular, so the tatpuruṣa fits.

morph.note: An epic (ārṣa) future built on the present stem इच्छ- (√इष् with the tudādi present इच्छति). The classical future of √इष् is एषिष्यति, which would give प्रत्येषिष्यामि; the Purāṇic form keeps the familiar present stem.
Instrumental of the present participle जानत् (√ज्ञा, kryādi, present stem जानी-/जान-). With the past participle कृताम् the doer stands in the instrumental: ‘done by one who knows’.

mantras.anvaya: जानता अजानता वा अपि तथा कृतां बलिपूजां तथा कृतं वह्निहोमं (च) अहं प्रीत्या प्रतीच्छिष्यामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject अहम्, verb प्रतीच्छिष्यामि, two objects each with a participle कृत; the instrumentals जानता / अजानता give the doer of both.
mantras.lit: Worship with offerings so performed, by one who knows or even by one who does not know, I will accept with love; and the fire oblation likewise performed.
mantras.tr: Whether the worship and offerings are made with knowledge or without it, I will accept them gladly, and the fire oblation too.
mantras.tr_note: तथा कृताम् is taken as ‘performed thus’, i.e. together with the recitation just prescribed in 12.10; the translation folds this into the sentence.

comm.t: Continuing 12.10: when the worship and the homa are accompanied by the recitation, the Devī accepts them with love whether the worshipper knows the correct procedure or not. Knowledge of ritual detail is not the condition of acceptance.
The tradition reads this as a promise that the recitation of the Saptaśatī makes good the defects of ritual performed in ignorance — which is why it is recited alongside other rites.
A modern reading: the Goddess here is no exacting examiner. Sincerity — the प्रीति that answers devotion — matters more than technical perfection.

flags.uncertain: तथा कृताम् / तथा कृतम्: तथा may mean ‘performed in that way’ (with the recitation of 12.10) or simply ‘likewise performed’; the first is followed. The future प्रतीच्छिष्यामि is non-classical (see Morph).

samasa.sense: in the autumn season (the months Āśvina and Kārttika)
samasa.alt: Also readable as a karmadhāraya, शरत् एव कालः ‘the season that is autumn’; the sense is the same.

samasa.sense: the great annual festival of the Goddess

morph.note: Passive present of √कृ: the root becomes क्रि- before the passive यक् (क्रि + य + ते).
वार्षिक, a taddhita derivative of वर्ष with vṛddhi of the first syllable and the affix -इक; feminine in -ई. It can mean ‘yearly’ (from वर्ष ‘year’) or ‘of the rains’ (from वर्षा).
Absolutive of √श्रु with क्त्वा; its subject is the person of 12.13 (मनुष्यः), whose main verb is भविष्यति.

mantras.anvaya: शरत्काले या च वार्षिकी महापूजा क्रियते, तस्यां मम एतत् माहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा भक्तिसमन्वितः (मनुष्यः) …
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (या … क्रियते) names the occasion; तस्याम् resumes it. The participial phrase ending in भक्तिसमन्वितः describes the subject of 12.13.
mantras.lit: And at the great worship which is performed in autumn, the annual one — at that, having heard this Māhātmya of mine, (a man) full of devotion …
mantras.tr: At the great yearly worship held in autumn, the one who hears this account of my glory with devotion

comm.t: The Devī singles out the great annual worship in autumn. Hearing the text then, with devotion, brings the fruits listed in the next verse.

This verse is the classic textual warrant for the Śāradīya Navarātra (Durgā Pūjā), the autumn festival in which the Saptaśatī is recited over nine nights; the aṣṭamī and navamī of 12.4 are its central days.

flags.uncertain: वार्षिकी is taken as ‘annual’ (from वर्ष ‘year’). It could also mean ‘belonging to the rainy season’ (from वर्षा); the tradition, which identifies the rite with the autumn Navarātra, follows ‘annual’.

samasa.alt: Also readable as a pañcamī tatpuruṣa, सर्वाबाधाभ्यः विनिर्मुक्तः; with words of release either case is used, and the sense is the same.

samasa.vigraha: धनं च धान्यं च सुताश्च धनधान्यसुताः (इतरेतरद्वन्द्वः); तैः अन्वितः
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing an itaretara dvandva
samasa.literal: joined with wealth, grain and sons

samasa.sense: by my grace; मद् (मत्) is the compound stem of the singular first-person pronoun

morph.note: Its last member विनिर्मुक्त is the past participle of वि + निर् + √मुच्; the two prefixes intensify ‘released’: ‘utterly freed’.
Future of √भू with two predicate nominatives (…विनिर्मुक्तः, …अन्वितः): ‘will become’.

mantras.anvaya: (तस्यां मम एतत् माहात्म्यं श्रुत्वा भक्तिसमन्वितः) मनुष्यः मत्प्रसादेन सर्वाबाधाविनिर्मुक्तः धनधान्यसुतान्वितः (च) भविष्यति; (अत्र) संशयः न (अस्ति)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause of the sentence begun in 12.12: subject मनुष्यः, verb भविष्यति, two predicate adjectives; then a short verbless clause, न संशयः.
mantras.lit: … a man, by my grace, will become freed from all afflictions and endowed with wealth, grain and sons; there is no doubt.
mantras.tr: will by my grace be freed from every trouble and blessed with wealth, grain and children. Of this there is no doubt.
mantras.tr_note: सुत (‘sons’) is rendered ‘children’ in the readable translation; the literal translation keeps ‘sons’.

comm.t: Completing 12.12: the devotee who hears the text at the autumn worship is freed from afflictions and prospers in wealth, grain and offspring — and the Devī adds her own guarantee, न संशयः.

The verse is among the best-known lines of the Saptaśatī and is widely recited on its own as a mantra for well-being and prosperity, for example as a sampuṭa (a line enclosing each verse) in a pāṭha undertaken for a particular wish. That use belongs to the later ritual tradition, not to the Purāṇa.
A modern reading: the blessing is concrete — freedom from trouble, food, family — and it is said to come ‘by my grace’ (मत्प्रसादेन), not as the automatic wage of a rite.

flags.uncertain: Variant: for the Gita Press धनधान्यसुतान्वितः, GRETIL and Freund read धनधान्यसमन्वितः (‘endowed with wealth and grain’, without ‘sons’); corrections.json marks it ‘Textual Verification Required’. The Gita Press reading, familiar from recitation, is analysed.
